- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior high), model often overshoots; cap forecast peak at 1–2% above prior high.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.10) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast mean.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3-day moving average before final forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 7-day average is > 10% above 30-day average, reduce forecast by 3–5%.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes, model tends to underestimate; adjust downward by 1–3% for each negative sentiment event.
